features: THE TOTAL ALWAYS ADDED UP — No migration: the database is not touched. This version comes from a forum report about millesimal tables and brought to light a money defect nobody had ever seen, for a reason worth telling.

A HEADING THAT DOES NOT DECLARE EVERYTHING NO LONGER CHARGES EVERYTHING. An expense heading is linked to millesimal tables with a percentage: it is the shape used to build fixed-share allocations, such as one third to whoever has exclusive use of the roof terrace and two thirds to the others. The program prevented those percentages from exceeding 100, but below that nobody was looking — and it distributed the whole expense onto the linked tables anyway. The concrete case: a € 9,000 roof terrace repair, you create the «exclusive use» table containing only the holder, link it at 33.33% and leave the other owners' table for later. Generating the plan at that moment, the holder received € 9,000 instead of € 3,000. Three times over, and no check said anything, because the plan's total matched the budget.

NOW THE UNDECLARED PART STAYS UNCOVERED: generation stops, says which heading and how much is missing, and you can go ahead all the same by writing down why — as already happens for a thousandth left blank. The last word stays the administrator's. If your headings are set up correctly nothing changes, and it has been verified: a three-way split adds up to 99.99 because of how percentages work, and it triggers nothing.

WHY NOBODY HAD EVER NOTICED. The engine turns an expense into shares through four proportions in a row, and at the end it renormalises: whatever is missing along the way, the total always comes back equal to the budget. That means this kind of defect does not show up as «the figures don't add up», but as money charged to the wrong person with the figures adding up perfectly. It is why they arrive from the forum one at a time rather than from our own checks: only someone actually managing a building can notice. Two of the four links are now closed; the other two are measured and will be closed together, because they are the same thing.

A DELIBERATE ZERO NOW REACHES THE PRINTOUT TOO. Since beta.61 you can write zero as a thousandth to say «this unit does not take part», typically in a table serving only part of the building: it serves to put on record that the unit was considered, so the table reads properly at the meeting. On the printed allocation that zero used to disappear — the cell came out with a dash, indistinguishable from a unit that is not in the table at all. It now writes 0.00 and is legible, where before it would have been the palest grey on a pale background. The amounts do not change by a cent: whoever is at zero still pays nothing, and those who take part split the expense exactly as before.

A NEGATIVE THOUSANDTH NO LONGER GETS IN THROUGH THE IMPORT. The ban existed for whoever fills in the screen, not for whoever imports a file. A «-900» — a typo, or a cell with accounting formatting read wrongly — gave no error, took no part in the allocation, but shrank the divisor: that table then weighed MORE than the percentage it was linked to the expense with, and the ones paying more were the other owners in that same table. On a € 1,000.00 expense split evenly between two tables, a single «-900» takes the share of someone with nothing to do with it from € 333.33 to € 484.85. The import now refuses it and writes it in the report. It does not correct it by itself: «-900» has no obvious right reading, and guessing would write into the archive a number that was not in the file.

WHAT YOU HAD ALREADY PAID IS NO LONGER ASKED FOR TWICE. An expense item may already be partly covered — a set-aside fund, an advance paid before the plan — and the program deducts it from the share. It did so in proportion to what that plan was asking against the budget, though, and from this version an expense can be asked for reduced: together, the two deducted only a fraction of what had already been paid. In the roof scenario — a € 9,000.00 item linked at only 33.33%, € 1,000.00 already paid — the plan asked for € 2,666.40, and inside that were € 666.70 already in the building's account. It now asks for € 1,999.70. The case the proportion exists for — an item paid in two tranches, an advance now and the balance in a few months — keeps working as before. The defect was already there for anyone with a unit without an owner on record or a table without thousandths, but it is this version that made the triggering case common, so it is fixed here.

TWO THINGS WE SAID AND DID NOT DO. «You can restrict a table to a stairwell or a block»: they could be chosen, they were saved, and no filter ever read them — whoever followed the instruction and ticked «link all existing properties» ended up with the whole building instead of just that stairwell's units. The panel and the sentence have been removed — along with the two other copies of the same promise in the buildings list, where what actually works is now written instead: you create a thousandths table containing only that block's units. The real filter is work planned for later. And the example of thousandths at zero cited the lift that ground floors supposedly do not pay for: that is not an explanation of the field, it is a legal qualification, and it is not that simple. The example now describes what the field does — the table of an installation or a stairwell serving only part of the building — and adds what matters: which units stay out is decided by the deed, not by the program.

UNDER THE HOOD: a new guard checks that every PDF document template actually opens, on every run of the automated checks. An error in a print template shows up nowhere — it does not go through the frontend build, and on-screen checking looks at screens — and the only way to notice was to open the PDF. Now a template that does not open stops the release instead of reaching the administrator.
